 Coram : R. D. Dhanuka &
 Gauri Godse, J
Dated : 16 March, 2023 P.C. :-
1.

Mr. Tulzapurkar, learned senior counsel for the Petitioners states that though in prayer clauses in the Petition his clients have prayed for quashing the Award dated 7th April 2022 and has prayed for Writ of Mandamus against the Respondent Authority to pass a fresh Award for compensation in lieu of acquisition of the land described in prayer clause (c) IRESH SIDDHARAM of the Petition, it is the case of the Petitioners that Award SIDDHARAM Date:
MASHAL 2023.03.18 ought to have been made under the provisions of Right to Fair 18:45:53 +0530 2/4 35.4890.22 wp.doc Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Act, 2013 ('2013 Act') and not under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.

He submitted that even if this Court comes to the conclusion that the Award is rightly made under the provisions of Land The Colaba Land And Mill Company Limited ... vs The State Of Maharashtra And 3 Ors on 16 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137876394/
1 Acquisition Act, 1894, the amount awarded in the impugned Award dated 7th April 2022 cannot be lesser than Rs.13,59,81,086/- which is deposited by Municipal Corporation with the Land Acquisition Officer.

sentences.text: Petitioner seeks liberty to withdraw the amount deposited by Municipal Corporation with Special Land Acquisition Officer on the ground that even if they fail, in view of Corporation not having challenged the Award, Petitioner would be entitled to withdraw at least the sum awarded in the Award dated 7th April 2022.

2. Mr. Godbole, learned senior counsel for Corporation on the other hand controverts the contentions raised by Mr. Tulzapurkar that Award ought to have been made under the provisions of the said 2013 Act on the ground that earlier Award granted by the Special Land Acquisition Officer was set aside by this Court with a direction to make a fresh Award and thus the land acquisition proceedings initiated under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 continues even after remission.

He also submitted that, in any event, if the Petitioner is aggrieved by the said Award by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, the Petitioners have remedy to file Reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act and in that event the issue whether the Award ought to have been made under the provisions of the said 2013 Act or not also can 3/4 35.4890.22 wp.doc be one of the issue,
subject to limitations prescribed under the provisions of the said 2013 Act.
3.

Learned counsel for Respondent No. 4 on the other hand seeks time to file affidavit-in-reply and place on record that Petitioners are not entitled to claim any amount under the amount Awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer in the Award dated 7th April 2022 on the ground that his clients are the owners of the said property.
He submitted that at some stage before passing of the Award, his clients raised the objections before Special Land Acquisition Officer, however, they were not considered.

He submitted in these circumstances, Petitioners cannot be allowed to withdraw any amount and if allowed, it will cause prejudice to the claims of compensation of Respondent No. 4 in the amount awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer by the said Award dated 7th April 2022.

4. Respondent No. 4 is granted two weeks time to file affidavit on the contentions raised by the Petitioners in the Writ Petition and also on the issue as to why the Petitioners cannot be allowed to withdraw the amount deposited by Municipal Corporation with the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
Copy of the reply shall be served upon learned Advocate for the Petitioners as well as upon Municipal Corporation simultaneously.
Rejoinder, if any, shall be filed within one week from the date of service of affidavit-in-reply.
5. Time granted to Municipal Corporation to file affidavit-in- 4/4 35.4890.22 wp.doc reply is extended by two weeks.
6. If the Competent Authority also proposes to file any reply, it shall be filed within two weeks from today and copy to be served upon learned counsel for the Petitioners.
Rejoinder, if any, to be filed within one week thereafter.
